raw_response:
I'm 67 this year, and I've been farming these same 3 mu in Quzhou since I was 22. Never spent a day in school, but I know my land like I know my own hands. My wife and me, we do all the work ourselves — no hired help, can't afford it, and anyway 3 mu is small enough for two old people if we work steady and don't rush.

The wheat went in last October, same as always. I used seed I kept from the harvest before last, cleaned it myself, didn't cost much more than a bit of my time. Before planting I ran the rotary tiller once and put down fertilizer — I bought two bags of compound fertilizer and one bag of urea from the shop in town, spread it by hand the way I always have. Now it's spring and the wheat is up and greening. I need to topdress soon when it starts jointing. I've got about half a bag of urea left in the shed from last year, and I'll spread that on the 3 mu. That's enough. Urea is over two yuan a jin now, and I need to save cash for the maize seed and fertilizer come June. My neighbor Old Wang down the road, he puts more on his wheat, but his son sends money home from the city. I don't have that.

I'll irrigate the wheat twice more: once at jointing, once when the heads come out. Pumping from the well costs me about 30 yuan each time for my 3 mu, but if I don't and the spring turns dry, the wheat will shrivel in the head. Last year we had decent rain and I only watered twice total, but you can't count on rain. Better to spend the money than lose the crop. I spray herbicide once in the spring if the weeds get bad — usually they do in the low spots. No insecticide unless I see worms with my own eyes.

Come early June, I'll cut the wheat. I hire the small combine by the mu — my back can't handle the scythe anymore. Then I have about five days, maybe a week, to get the maize in before the season slips away. I'll rotary till once right after harvest, then plant. I buy hybrid maize seed from the agricultural shop — need about 3 to 4 jin for 3 mu. For maize fertilizer, I put one bag of compound and about one bag of urea in the row at planting. When the maize is knee-high, I topdress with another half bag of urea. Maize doesn't need as much fuss as wheat if the summer rain comes. I irrigate maybe twice — once when it's tasseling, once when the ears are filling. If it's a wet summer, maybe only once.

I don't keep precise books in my head, but I know I can't spend too much. My wife and me, we need to keep some cash aside for medicine and food. If I put too much fertilizer on and then one of us gets sick, we're in trouble. I aim for about 400 jin per mu for wheat and about the same for maize — last year I got close to that. I'm not trying to break records, just trying to get through the year steady. I've seen too many farmers go broke chasing high yields.
